title: Chapter 289: Body Inside the Peach Plantation
html:
A fleeting flash of light made the dangling head even more terrifying. Slender hands crowded the window, fingers curling over every edge. Yet at that critical moment, Chen Ge’s thoughts were elsewhere.

The woman’s face is similar to the spider monster drawn by Fan Yu. She doesn’t look old; it fits perfectly. She should be Jiang Ling’s older sister.

The wooden beams creaked, and the entire hut shuddered as though it might collapse beneath the pressure. Spiderwebs crept toward Chen Ge while the woman forced her head through the opening. “Save me! Save me!”

“That’s exactly why I came!” Chen Ge dared not wait until the situation spiraled out of control. The answer appeared to catch the woman by surprise. She fell silent but continued squeezing inside. Bloodred webbing clung to the walls as conflicting emotions distorted her face.

“You’re Jiang Ling’s sister; we’ve met before!” The woman remained unmoved, as though she did not understand him. “Jiujiang Children’s Home! Don’t you remember?”

Chen Ge was ready to summon Xu Yin when he remembered the bottle in his pocket. He held it up. “Your little sister gave me this!”

Inside lay the crushed spider Jiang Ling had presented to him at the Children’s Home. The hut stopped shaking. The woman’s pupil-less eyes settled on the bottle, and her attack on the window ceased. After studying Chen Ge for a moment, she stretched her head toward him.

Her pale neck was twice the length of a human being’s. Chen Ge unscrewed the bottle and offered it with one hand. The terrifying creature finally calmed. She closed her mouth and appeared to consider his intentions.

“I mean you no harm. You and your sister have suffered terribly, and I came to help.” Chen Ge quietly switched off the recorder. “Your sister told me a great deal. I understand your circumstances and your pain. In a sense, we’re alike; I’ve endured despair too.”

He had once said much the same to Xu Yin. Social grace was not Chen Ge’s strength, so all he could do was put himself in another’s place. Human and ghost stared at each other through the wall between them.

“I’ll help you clear your name, and I’ll take care of your family!

“Why do you think I entered the mountain alone in the middle of the night?

“I only want to help your little sister, who desperately wishes to ease your pain!”

By the end, even Chen Ge believed every word. His expression was solemn, his voice weighted with pain. The woman drew back and tilted her head. Her anger had faded, replaced by confusion.

“I can help you release your resentment and leave this place of suffering. I can give you a new home,” Chen Ge said earnestly.

The woman seemed to be beginning to trust him. Though she did not fully understand his words, she shook her head the moment he suggested taking her away.

“I know you love your sister and want to protect her, but your presence causes other children to bully her. They see her as a monster, a patient. She cannot live normally, form ordinary attachments, or allow herself to be loved.

“I can understand you, but others can’t. Believe me, if you continue to shadow her, one day, you’ll become her darkest nightmare!

“Do you want to hear from your own sister’s lips that she hates you?!”

The conversation had clearly gone somewhere the woman never expected. Her white eyes rolled before she shook her head again.

“I won’t force you to choose. I’m only telling you the truth for your own sake.” An indescribable sorrow entered Chen Ge’s voice. “I have experienced the pain you endured and the pain still waiting for you. If you ever have nowhere else to go, come and find me.”

Then he made a daring gesture. Keeping the hammer hidden behind his back in his right hand, he extended his left toward her. “My little brother is your little sister’s best friend. Perhaps you and I could become friends too.”

He made no effort to lower his voice. A strange thump came from next door, as though someone had fallen out of bed. The woman’s eyes rolled wildly. She leaned away, staring at his extended hand.

“We really can.” Chen Ge stepped forward. Her eyes spun even faster, and she spat a strand of webbing across the door before retreating into the orchard and vanishing.

“Wait!” Chen Ge shoved aside the bed and rushed outside, but the woman was gone. I didn’t even give her my address… Never mind. This was a promising beginning. If I want her to join the Haunted House, I’ll have to persuade her through Jiang Ling.

The neighboring door flew open, and Master Bai rushed out clutching his lamp and hoe. He stood trembling in the doorway, genuinely terrified of Chen Ge. What kind of man encountered a ghost without fear, then opened his door and chased after it with regret on his face?

“Master Bai, you’ve been eavesdropping, right?”

Rain plastered Chen Ge’s hair to his forehead. When he faced Master Bai, the old man quivered beneath his gaze.

What is he going to do? Kill me to silence me? Also, where did he find that hammer that looks like a murder weapon?!

“No. You were talking in your sleep and woke me. Since you’re unharmed, I’ll return to bed.” Master Bai clutched the hoe so tightly that veins bulged across his hands. His lips trembled with nerves.

“There’s no point lying anymore. This is a crime scene. A family of four lived here: the parents were poisoned, the elder daughter disappeared, and I believe she was the creature I just saw.”

Chen Ge thought about it before adding, “She disappeared into the peach plantation, and when I first met you, you were digging inside the plantation. If my guess is correct, you should have been searching for her body.”

Master Bai froze. After a long silence, he asked in a voice heavy with guilt and regret, “How did you discover that?”

“Not only do I know that you’re looking for her body, I also know that her body is hidden under the tallest tree at the plantation.” Chen Ge pointed at the blood red spider web on the door. It was the clue left behind by the woman.
